name: NY-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+25 partisan lean makes it one of the most Democratic seats in the country
Claire Valdez has raised about $1.7 million with $1.2 million in outside support; Republican Melvin Rivera reports no measurable fundraising
Open seat after Nydia Velázquez's retirement is the main residual uncertainty
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 97 percent
model.rationale: The seat's D+25 lean, Valdez's overwhelming financial advantage over a little-funded Republican opponent, and market pricing near certainty all point to the district staying in Democratic hands despite the open-seat transition.
model.watch: Any late surge in Republican or independent spending, or an unexpected scandal in the Democratic campaign, would be the first sign of movement in a race that currently shows none.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Nydia Velázquez (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
New York's seventh district is among the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 25 points Democratic. Nydia Velázquez's retirement leaves an open seat, but Democratic nominee Claire Valdez enters the general election with a large financial edge: about $1.7 million raised plus roughly $1.2 million in outside support, and no outside spending against her. Republican Melvin Rivera reports no measurable fundraising, and independent Priscilla Ghaznavi has raised under $40,000.

No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters cover the race. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 97 percent. The district's heavy Democratic lean, the stark money imbalance, and market pricing all point to the seat remaining in Democratic hands, with the open-seat transition the main source of residual uncertainty.
